news.title: Uefa calls emergency meeting as opposition to Fifa plan hardens
news.lede: 55 members to meet on Thursday to coordinate response. ‘Uefa knows there is significant and growing opposition’. Uefa has called an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members for Thursday afternoon to discuss a coordinated response to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A European boycott of Fifa tournaments is among the options under consideration.

news.title: Infantino calls plan to sell World Cup stake a proposal, 'not an obligation'
news.lede: FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - FIFA World Cup 2026 Draw - John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, Washington, D.C., U.S. - December 5, 2025 FIFA President Gianni Infantino arrives on the red carpet ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Draw REUTERS/Brian Snyder/File Photo. July 29 - FIFA President Gianni Infantino called the plan to sell stakes in the World Cup a proposal but 'not an obligation' after the idea provoked a furious response from some football authorities. FIFA announced plans this week to create a $20 billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and its other events, and said it will offer stakes of up to 20% in it to external investors.

news.title: Infantino’s World Cup plan is part of a desire for expansion that was clear from the start | Paul MacInnes
news.lede: Fifa’s plans to sell a share of the World Cup’s commercial rights are the latest in a long line of presidential power moves. In hindsight, it was all in the open from the very off. When Gianni Infantino was first elected as president of Fifa in 2016 it was something of a shock victory and prompted hope for progress after the dark days of Sepp Blatter. Infantino had promised to restore “the image of Fifa”, but also anticipated that “everyone in the world will applaud us”.

news.title: Cape Verde's World Cup hero Vozinha hit by bizarre rule that could wipe his famous name off his shirt
news.lede: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha is set to begin the next chapter of his career with Chilean giants Colo-Colo, but the name that made him one of the breakout stars of the 2026 FIFA World Cup may not appear on the back of his shirt. Football News: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, a breakout star of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, may not have his famous nickname on his Colo-Colo jersey due to Chilean league regulations prohibiting nicknames. Discover the potential implications of this rule and the club's efforts to secure an exemption.

news.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
news.lede: Players held banner after semi-final against England. Paredes and Molina investigated over brawl after final. Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falklands Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta. As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

news.title: FIFA's World Cup sale plan met with shock and anger
news.lede: A proposal that could reshape the commercial future of the World Cup has sparked fierce opposition from football's governing bodies. FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday unveiled plans to create a $20 billion (€17.5 billion) company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to run competitions including the World Cup and Club World Cup with private investors, according to The Times of London. Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter voiced concern over the close ties between Infantino and US President Donald Trump, as Thrive Eternal, led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, is among the reported potential investors. Meanwhile, EU Commissioner for Sport Glenn Micallef wrote on X: "Hands off our game."

news.title: ‘It is not FIFA’s to sell’ - Gianni Infantino’s $20 billion World Cup power play puts soccer’s soul up for sale - and makes resistance too expensive
news.lede: Gianni Infantino’s move to sell stakes in FIFA’s commercial rights is part of a disheartening trend stripping the soul from professional sports. Earlier this week, Gianni Infantino got a little bit angry. In a 15-slide Instagram post, the FIFA President took on all of the criticism of the 2026 World Cup. It was, effectively, a laundry list of his accomplishments, accompanied, pointedly, by counterarguments to every single pre-tournament grievance.

news.title: World Cup: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino offers £30m incentive for members to back controversial private investment plans
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has given football associations until September 19 to back his plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors with a £30.1m ($40m) incentive to accept, a letter has revealed. FIFA announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments. Under the proposal, FIFA would raise up to £3.1bn ($4.2bn) from external investors by selling minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it says would be valued at around £15bn ($20bn). The governing body says its plans - which need approval from member associations - could deliver more than £7.53bn ($10bn) in "football development funding" over the next four years.
